Parent interview notes

Before you begin

Explain and record consent

Required

Read the short script aloud. The participant may skip any question or stop. Audio recording is optional; anonymous note-taking permission is required to save interview notes.

“Thank you for speaking with me. I’m researching what families near Chawkbazar and Percival Hill need from after-school Qur’an and Arabic learning for children. This is not an enrollment pitch, and there are no right answers. The conversation should take about 45 minutes. You can skip any question or stop at any time. I’ll take notes without using your name. May I take notes? Would you be comfortable with an audio recording for note accuracy? Recording is optional.”
Use a code only; do not enter the parent’s or child’s name.

01 · Current experience

Routine and current choices

10 min
Where do lessons happen, how often, and who manages transport or pickup?
What triggered the search? Which options did you consider, and what made you choose or reject them?
What feedback do you receive? What would you like to know that you do not know today?
02 · Goals and decision criteria

Needs, trust, and schedule

15 min
What would reassure you that new memorization is balanced with retention? What pace or teaching behavior would worry you?
Explore reading, Qur’anic vocabulary, understanding simple phrases, and spoken conversation. Which would you prioritize first, and why?
Possible probes: teacher experience, group size, child protection, arrival/pickup, gender arrangements, room visibility, communication.
School dismissal, traffic, transport, prayer times, caregiver work, siblings, homework, and rest.
03 · Show the concept now

Reaction to Iqra

10 min

Iqra — Qur’an & Arabic Learning Centre

A specialist after-school program for ages 5–12. Hifz and Arabic are tracked separately. Children are placed by current level. Hifz includes new memorization and planned revision, with pace based on mastery and no fixed completion-time promise. Arabic milestones cover reading, vocabulary, comprehension, and speaking. Proposed fixed batches are 3:00–5:00 pm and 5:10–7:10 pm, five days per week. Each session is planned as 80 minutes Hifz, 30 minutes Arabic, and a 10-minute break. Maximum 20 students per batch; Hifz group maximum 10 students per teacher. Admission would include a placement assessment and one trial session. Fees and opening date are not set.
